1.
Leave granted.
2.  The proceedings in this case commence with the issuance of a notification under the National Highways Act, 1956 for the acquisition of land of the appellant.
By order dated 28.02.2007, the Land Acquisition Collector (LAC) gave compensation of Rs 55,785/- @ Rs 37,190/- per marla.
Being aggrieved, the appellant filed an application for enhancement of land compensation before the LAC.

3. The matter was then referred for adjudication through arbitration and the learned Arbitrator by an award dated 20.04.20111 awarded the following amounts: (a) Price of land was enhanced to Rs 4.5 lakhs per marla; (b) Compensation of shop @ Rs 400/- per Sq.ft; (c) Business loss @ Rs. 1.50 lakh lumpsum; (d) Compensation towards shifting of Malba @ Rs 20,000/- lump sum; (e) solatium to be paid as per Land Acquisition Act, 1894; and (f) Interest @ 9% p.a.
4.
The respondents challenged the Award under Section 34 of 18:06:03 IST the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 19962.
The District Judge allowed the appeal and remanded the matter back to the 1
For short the Award.
2 For short the Act.
learned Arbitrator for re-determination.
This remand order was challenged by the appellant under Section 37 of the Act before the High Court of Punjab and Haryana3.

sentences.text: 5. The High Court by its order impugned before us, partly allowed the appeal and confined the award to Rs. 4.5 lakhs per marla.
The justification for allowing the appeal was only that another appeal under Section 37 of the Act, arising out of a similar case, was allowed by the High Court.

In that similar case, it is to be seen that the award itself was confined to Rs. 4.5 lakhs per marla and the Rakesh Kumar vs Union Of India on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66639650/

sentences.text: High Court confined its determination to the awarded amount.
6. The point of distinction is very clear.
In this case apart from Rs 4.5 lakhs per marla, the Award also grants distinct amounts towards compensation, business loss, shifting of malba, solatium and interest, as indicated hereinabove.

In this view of the matter, there was no justification for Courts adjudicating petitions under Sections 34 and 37 of the Act to vary the award without examining if there exists any patent illegality in the making of the Award.

7. In view of the above, we allow Civil Appeal No. 4905 of 2024 and set aside the judgment of the High Court4.
8.
The appellant shall be entitled to the entirety of the amount as awarded in his favour by virtue of the award dated 20.04.2011 passed by the learned Arbitrator.
